claims.text: Replacing full AIMD sampling with ML-assisted thermodynamic integration will reduce computational cost.
The ML-assisted method will preserve free-energy fidelity for both solid and fluid states.
The MLIP will be trained on a sparse high-temperature AIMD dataset spanning solid and liquid phases.
The trained MLIP will enable extensive free-energy sampling.
Periodic on-the-fly ab initio corrections through thermodynamic perturbation theory will retain vibrational entropy accurately.
Periodic on-the-fly ab initio corrections will retain anharmonic effects accurately.
Periodic on-the-fly ab initio corrections will retain electron–vibration coupling accurately.
Ab initio free-energy sampling has previously been validated for elemental and binary metals near fusion conditions.
Replica exchange or advanced path sampling can be used with the MLIP to compute free energies and relevant entropy terms.
Short AIMD recalibration snippets can correct drift in the MLIP.
The intended operating range extends from just below to above melting and typically up to approximately 3000 K for metals.
An error below 5 meV/atom in energy differences is proposed as an acceptable accuracy target relative to full AIMD.
Reproducing local chemical environments and fluctuations in both phases will maintain the fidelity of vibrational entropy and anharmonicity.
ML-potential sampling over longer timescales and broader phase-space regions will drastically reduce the cost of sampling free-energy differences.
Cheaper empirical potentials often lose electron–vibration coupling and subtle entropy contributions.
The proposed method will cost one to two orders of magnitude less than full explicit AIMD workflows.
The proposed method will be faster than TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will retain fidelity comparable to explicit AIMD for free energies and derived observables.
The method is expected to be reliable for elemental and binary systems when suitable AIMD reference data are available.
Application to multicomponent high-entropy systems may fail if the training data or ML descriptors do not capture their phase-space variations and electron–vibration coupling.
